**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Unbind the transport when context validation fails**

When an authenticated OAuth client uses a `client_id` rejected by the new schema, such as whitespace-only or more than 256 characters, `createConnectionContext()` throws here after `bindings.bind()` has installed the mapping but before the cleanup `try` block begins. This is reachable because `src/oauth.ts` accepts any nonempty `client_id`; no session is persisted, yet another open attempt on the same transport fails with `TRANSPORT_BINDING_CONFLICT`. Construct and validate the context before binding, or include record construction in the cleanup block.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed on exact head `81832e1b702a8dfe10cda5634d6092fb3a177142` with the minimal side-effect ordering change: `createConnectionContext(...)` is now constructed/validated before `TransportBindings.bind(...)`, so malformed OAuth client metadata fails before any transport mutation. A dedicated regression test was added and registered in the existing read-only safety suite. TDD evidence: RED on head `f3b4bacd1d8a6975d33c949372cda6f1d1d2d523` / MCP CI #711 showed exactly 271/272 passing with the leaked binding as the sole failure; GREEN on head `81832e1b702a8dfe10cda5634d6092fb3a177142` / MCP CI #713 now passes 272/272, including `openSession releases the transport binding when ConnectionContext validation fails`, plus typecheck, build, docs/governance, secret scan and whitespace checks. No parallel cleanup mechanism or authority was added.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Put the closure merge SHA first in SUIVI**

After this documentation commit is merged and deployed, `buildDocumentationLiveStateCommand()` reads the first 40-character SHA in `SUIVI.md` as `declaredGithubSha`, so this line selects the PR #68 head `81832e1...`, while the first `S1 HEAD` line declares `c87598d...`. Because `parseDocumentationObservation()` exempts a docs-only descendant from the S1 mismatch only when both declared SHAs are equal, the newly deployed S1 SHA will be reported as `DOCUMENTATION_DRIFT`, preventing the intended `FULLY_ALIGNED` closure. Place `c87598d...` before the PR head evidence, as the previous checkpoint did, so both declarations use the same ancestor.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate `find` failures through the pipeline**

When `/var/www/vhosts` is missing or unreadable, or `find` otherwise fails during traversal, stderr is discarded and the pipeline returns `head`'s successful exit status because pipefail is not enabled. `collectServedDomains()` therefore treats the resulting empty or partial output as `CURRENT`, which can incorrectly produce `DOMAIN_NONE_CONFIRMED`; make the producer's failure propagate before accepting the inventory.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope the observation to the selected project**

On a multi-tenant S1, this passes every valid Plesk vhost to GW-09 for whichever single project is currently resolved. `resolveDomain()` compares those entries with only that project's declarations and returns `DOMAIN_OBSERVATION_UNDECLARED` as soon as another project's domain is present, so no selected project can reach `RESOLVED` or confirmed `NONE` on a shared server; the observation must be scoped to the target project, or the resolver must exclude domains belonging to other registry projects.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Confirmed. Fixed in `469dd79` (not yet pushed): the default C5 reader now scopes the Live State observation to the domains GitRegistry declares for the selected project on that server (`declaredProjectDomains` + `scopeDomainObservation`), so another tenant's vhost no longer reads as `DOMAIN_OBSERVATION_UNDECLARED`. Test: `the observation is scoped to the selected project on a shared server`.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep observation evidence independent of declarations**

Fresh evidence after the earlier shared-server correction: because every retained entry must satisfy `declared.has(...)`, the default reader can never deliver an undeclared entry to GW-09. In particular, a project declaring no domains produces an available empty observation and `DOMAIN_NONE_CONFIRMED`, even though collection only observed an unscoped shared-server inventory and established no project ownership; this also makes `DOMAIN_OBSERVATION_UNDECLARED` unreachable through the default path. Scope using independent Plesk project/subscription evidence, or leave the observation unavailable when ownership cannot be established.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include names served as aliases in the inventory**

When a declared public domain is a Plesk alias, listing only `system/<directory>` basenames can miss a binding that is actively served by another vhost, causing GW-09 to return `DOMAIN_DECLARATION_UNOBSERVED`. Plesk documents that [domain aliases point multiple names to the same website](https://docs.plesk.com/en-US/obsidian/administrator-guide/website-management/websites-and-domains/domains-and-dns/adding-domain-aliases.65286/) and its [vhost example serves `www.domainXX.tst` through `ServerAlias`](https://docs.plesk.com/en-US/obsidian/advanced-administration-guide-linux/virtual-hosts-configuration/virtual-hosts-and-hosting-types.68694/), so directory names alone are not a complete served-name inventory; include bounded alias data from Plesk or the active webserver configuration.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Valid gap, not fixed in this PR. The failure is closed: a declared domain served only as a Plesk alias reads `DOMAIN_DECLARATION_UNOBSERVED`, which is `UNVERIFIED` — a false negative, never a false positive `RESOLVED`/`NONE`. Inventorying aliases means parsing per-vhost webserver configuration (`server_name`/`ServerAlias`), a broader read I'd rather add as its own F-04 increment than widen this one. Recorded as a known limit in SUIVI.md.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check Plesk status before certifying a served domain**

When a declared domain is suspended or disabled in Plesk, this directory scan can still return its basename even though it is no longer an active served vhost: Plesk documents that changing website status does not remove the related server content, while active nginx vhosts are represented separately by include links into the `system/<domain>/conf` tree ([website status](https://docs.plesk.com/en-US/obsidian/administrator-guide/website-management/websites-and-domains/hosting-settings/general-settings/website-status.72339/), [configuration hierarchy](https://docs.plesk.com/en-US/obsidian/administrator-guide/web-servers/apache-and-nginx-web-servers-linux/apache-and-nginx-configuration-files.68678/)). Directory presence alone therefore cannot prove active status, yet the result is later marked `verified: true`, allowing GW-09 to return `RESOLVED` from retained administrative files; inventory active includes or query Plesk status and fail closed otherwise.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate Punycode labels instead of matching their prefix**

When the Plesk output contains a fake A-label such as `example.xn--a` or `example.xn--foo-`, this regex accepts it and the parser returns a `CURRENT` inventory; if GitRegistry contains the same malformed value, it can consequently be emitted as a verified resolved domain. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Age each inventory from its own observation time**

When one server's query completes quickly but the other server's parallel SSH query stalls, the first inventory was observed at the timestamp recorded by `collectServedDomains`, yet this projection replaces it with the later snapshot reconciliation time and calculates freshness from that later time. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound the Plesk query before streaming its output**

On a Plesk server with more than 1000 active names, this SQL statement still materializes and streams every matching domain and alias on every Live State cycle. `parseServedDomainInventory()` rejects an over-limit result and the SSH client caps retained bytes, but neither stops MySQL or the SSH channel from producing the remaining rows, so a deliberately bounded inventory can consume unbounded database, network, and callback work until the 30-second timeout. Cap the SQL result at 1001 rows so the parser can detect overflow without reading the full inventory.

Fresh evidence after the earlier concurrency correction: when either new served-domain SSH read consumes its 30-second timeout while the GitHub, S1, or runtime read finishes promptly, `Promise.all` still waits for that timeout and reconciliation assigns every source the later `lastReconciledAt`; those source types have no individual timestamp, and consumers such as `liveStateRuntimeObservation()` age them from that later value, so stale evidence can remain `CURRENT` for roughly 30 extra seconds. Concurrency limits total collection time but does not preserve observation time; retain timestamps per source or reconcile freshness from the earliest completed observation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Traced, not changed in this PR. Live State has always stamped every source with the one `lastReconciledAt`: the existing S1 head, runtime and current-state inventory reads already go through `runReadOnlyCommand` with the same 30 s SSH timeout inside the same `Promise.all`, so a slow existing read already delays the stamp by up to 30 s. The served-domain reads run concurrently with them and use the same bound, so they do not raise that worst case. Per-source observation timestamps would change Live State's snapshot model for every consumer, which is a separate change; the served-domain observation itself already ages from its own `observedAt`. Leaving this open for the owner's call.
